title: Office ownership is instance-blind, so one lane tears down another lane's in-flight conversion (harness-reachable only)
detail: The CanvasDownloaderTmp marker means 'some Canvas Downloader', not 'this instance', so a lane's teardown reads another lane's staged conversion document as ours-and-discardable, quits, waits 12s, then pkills the app mid-conversion. Measured 0.77s from free3's force-terminate to the office lane's -609. Requires two concurrent instances, which start.py's flock/mutex prevents for normal users and the harness creates by design - so this is recorded as a HARNESS-BLOCKING robustness gap, not a user-facing defect. Blocks trustworthy Office rows in any multi-lane matrix; workaround is to run the converting lane alone.

evidence.reachability: TWO CONCURRENT INSTANCES ONLY. start.py's flock/mutex blocks a second GUI, and within one instance conversions are sequential with teardown after them. Not reachable for a normal user. It IS reachable in the audit harness, which runs 5 instances by design.
causation_measured_to_under_a_second: free3  14:59:54.043  [OfficeQuit] force-terminated Microsoft PowerPoint (no user documents open)
office 14:59:54.812  [AppleScript] PowerPoint was not usable (-609) - it most likely crashed or was torn down mid-conversion; relaunching and retrying src_bc80f7.pptx once
sequence: 1. a free lane finishes a row and runs teardown

3. quit saving no reports '1 open doc(s), none user-owned' - that doc is the OFFICE lane's staged conversion document, which carries the shared CanvasDownloaderTmp marker and so reads as ours-and-discardable
4. PowerPoint does not exit (it is busy converting) -> _wait_for_exit times out at 12s
5. escalate -> _terminate_gallery_stuck -> pkill -x, which runs OUTSIDE the per-app lock
6. the office lane's conversion dies with -609 / -600

two_parts.a: pkill -x in _terminate_gallery_stuck runs outside _office_app_lock. The comment justifying that ('signalling a process is not driving it') is wrong: killing the app another instance is converting with is more destructive than driving it.
two_parts.b: THE REAL ONE: the CanvasDownloaderTmp marker identifies 'some Canvas Downloader', not THIS instance. Instance B inspects instance A's in-flight staged document, concludes ours-not-user-owned, and clears it for quitting. Fixing (a) alone is insufficient because the already-locked 'quit saving no' at step 3 still closes the other instance's document.

evidence.harness_impact: 5 office rows corrupted in run 20260821_144948 (m012,m013,m014,m025,m026). m025 alone: 6 crash-recoveries and 4 outright conversion failures (-50, -30001). The -30001 'frontmost presentation is not the one Canvas Downloader opened' entries are the app's OWN guard working correctly after a crash-recovery deck came frontmost - a downstream symptom, not a second defect.
evidence.why_it_matters_operationally: While unfixed, any download matrix with a converting lane plus any other live lane produces Office failures that are indistinguishable from product defects in the row's own findings - the trap CLAUDE.md already records.
evidence.workaround_in_use: Run the converting lane alone; no concurrency, no contention.
evidence.related: fp:db1a2417c30a (the lock coverage gap, fixed in 2ca557b) - same area, and (b) is why that fix was necessary but not sufficient.
